# Code review

## Trigger and inputs

Use this Skill for independent, source-read-only review of actual changed work, its approved Plan, inspected implementation report, original criteria and validation evidence. Follow the [review rubric](./review-rubric.md) and use the [Review report template](./review-report-template.md) for prospective durable reports. This Skill itself grants no edit, command, lifecycle, approval, delegation or acceptance authority.

## Procedure

1. Inspect Plan/report versions and direct physical same-folder lineage, actual diff and principal artifact. Establish the intended implementation range from available baseline/Plan/report evidence, then inspect the full relevant change set and remaining work—not merely the latest commit or report. When range/baseline facts are unavailable, continue bounded investigation and record the gap; do not guess coverage. Compare changed work to original acceptance, security, compatibility and least-privilege boundaries; commits are evidence aids, not scope/approval or proof of complete delivery, and a saved report alone is not delivery. Assess the approved Plan's checkpoint strategy/approval reference and expected Work Item/Task opportunities, including reported no-commit paths; distinguish observed timely completion-to-save/readback, observed late/omitted actions, and unverified timing. Silence or final markers cannot establish chronology or compliance, and a missing commit alone is not a technical defect.
	Independently assess complete architectural choice coverage against Research, the approved Plan and actual changes, including missing or partial coverage even when a valid ADR is bound. Verify each choice's rationale, alternatives, selection/pending state, conditions and affected Work Items against inspected existing/grouped coverage; a vague umbrella record is insufficient. For unexpected uncovered or changed architecture, require engineer-directed Plan resolution before dependent architectural effects; continue independent approved work. Routine naming, helper extraction and architecture-preserving repairs remain Implement-owned without ADR reference; resolve material classification ambiguity with the engineer using evidence.
	When the Plan binds an ADR, independently inspect its exact bound path/ID, section, substantive version/preimage and current state. Compare the implementation report's actual invocation and per-record persistence evidence with the physical ADR postimage and agreement/conditions; do not infer `Accepted` from invocation alone or assume an unverified save succeeded. A prior `/implement` invocation is not retroactive if the exact-snapshot rule was not effective before it. Do not infer architectural agreement or enterprise approval from Plan invocation, implementation, or clean delivery Review. Review gains no ADR authorship or status-write authority.
2. Record evidence-backed findings with precise location, impact, severity and smallest supported correction. Classify **severity**, **actionability/uncertainty**, and **original-criteria correction versus material change** separately. Avoid stylistic-only or duplicate findings.
3. Continue investigating factual uncertainty; retain unclear findings when evidence is insufficient. Mixed supported and unclear findings permit independent supported correction but prevent acceptance until every unresolved finding is settled. `Blocker` is severity, not a phase status.
4. For supported in-boundary corrections, offer manual resumption of Implement with the original approved Plan and linked Review context; findings supply evidence, not edit authority or new scope. Require fresh implementation evidence and fresh independent Review. Material new requirements, public behavior, dependencies, security/compatibility commitments or external effects require engineer choice and Plan-owned amendment/new Plan; renew Research only if new evidence requires it.
5. Do not edit source, delegate fixes or self-accept. `/review` admits assessment, not acceptance; a clean, physically verified evidence-backed Review with no unresolved findings records acceptance. Optional status bookkeeping cannot substitute for it.

## Output and validation

### Checkpoint planning and boundary assessment

Apply the [shared checkpoint capability](../local-git-checkpoints/SKILL.md). Assess every prospective Plan for one explicit bounded strategy and every detailed Work Item for a strategy reference, normal post-validation boundary and coherent content/purpose, or a specific justified combination/deferral/no-commit exception. Each exception must identify the actual constraint/reason, affected IDs, validation/dependency consequence, later boundary if one exists and why the normal boundary is unsuitable. Missing entries, empty headings, generic exemptions and unexplained blanket bans fail planning assessment; actual prohibitions, including historical Plans, still grant no Git authority. Do not demand historical rewrites or fabricate future obstacles.

Compare planned versus actual accounting for every expected boundary before unrelated work, including consideration of earlier coherent validated Tasks. Require actual disposition evidence, not a session-end summary of commit count. Assess omissions and unjustified departures with citations; runtime obstacles belong in fresh implementation evidence, not retrospective substantive approved-Plan exceptions. Distinguish verified checkpoints from supported skips, not attempted, unavailable/unresolved, failed, no commit verified, unexpected effects and uncertain completion; preserve reconciliation and all runtime safeguards. Distinguish observed timely handling, observed late/omitted handling and unverified chronology; silence, final history or markers do not prove timing. Commit count is not technical acceptance; a supported no-commit outcome is not defective delivery. This assessment grants no Git effects, substantive Plan edits or acceptance by itself.

Return cited, severity-ranked findings with actionable/unclear and correction/material classification, or a supported clean result. State checks **Performed**, **Failed**, **Unavailable**, **Not run** separately. Preserve physical lineage, non-overwriting record saves and full readback where the coordinator persists a report; a failed save is not persisted. Keep handoffs manual and preserve finalized historical evidence.
